report.name: COREP C72.00 — Liquidity Coverage Ratio
report.description: Monthly Liquidity Coverage Ratio: the stock of high-quality liquid assets over stressed 30-day net cash outflows. HQLA is built in SQL; the stressed outflow leg is computed in a SAS engine with a runtime stress scenario.

table.caption: C72.00 — Liquidity Coverage Ratio by stress scenario (reporting month 2026-09)

cdes.definition: Stock of unencumbered high-quality liquid assets divided by total net cash outflows over a 30-day stress horizon, expressed as a percentage.

candidates.why: Final COREP output; percentage form of the mart ratio and matches the C72.00 cell.
Mart ratio one hop upstream, before rescaling to percent.

cdes.expected_story: LCR = total HQLA ÷ stressed net outflows. HQLA is a fully-traceable SQL haircut calculation; the outflow leg is computed in SAS, so that branch of the field trace stops at the SAS boundary until the AI layer reads it.

cdes.aggregation_level: Entity level (SUM of post-haircut security values)
cdes.definition: Total value of unencumbered liquid assets after supervisory haircuts, eligible for the liquidity buffer.

candidates.why: Sum of post-haircut HQLA values; fully traceable through SQL to raw security market values.

cdes.expected_story: total_hqla_eur = SUM(market_value × (1 − haircut)). A fully-traceable SQL calculation from raw securities.

cdes.aggregation_level: Entity level (SUM of stressed deposit outflows)
cdes.definition: Total expected cash outflows less capped inflows over a 30-day combined stress scenario.

candidates.why: Aggregates the SAS outflow engine; the per-deposit formula is opaque until the AI layer reads the DATA step.

cdes.expected_story: outflow_eur = balance × runoff_rate × stress_factor, computed in a SAS DATA step with a runtime scenario. The field trace stops at the SAS boundary until the AI layer recovers the formula.

code.text:
-- Securities master (system of record)
CREATE TABLE raw.securities (
  isin                VARCHAR PRIMARY KEY,
  asset_class         VARCHAR,
  market_value_eur    DECIMAL(18,2),
  regulatory_haircut  DECIMAL(5,4),
  encumbered_flag     SMALLINT
);

-- Deposit system (system of record)
CREATE TABLE raw.deposits (
  deposit_id         VARCHAR PRIMARY KEY,
  counterparty_type  VARCHAR,
  balance_eur        DECIMAL(18,2),
  product_type       VARCHAR,
  insured_flag       SMALLINT
);

-- ALM runtime stress scenario set
CREATE TABLE liq.stress_scenarios (
  scenario_id       VARCHAR,
  scenario_name     VARCHAR,
  runoff_multiplier DECIMAL(5,4),
  inflow_cap_pct    DECIMAL(5,4)
);

-- 01_stage_hqla.sql  ·  post-haircut HQLA values
CREATE TABLE stg.hqla_securities AS
SELECT
    isin,
    asset_class,
    market_value_eur,
    regulatory_haircut,
    -- HQLA value after supervisory haircut
    market_value_eur * (1 - regulatory_haircut) AS hqla_value_eur,
    CASE WHEN encumbered_flag = 0
         AND asset_class IN ('L1','L2A','L2B')
         THEN 1 ELSE 0 END                      AS eligible_flag
FROM raw.securities
WHERE encumbered_flag = 0;

-- 01_stage_deposits.sql  ·  deposit book with base runoff rates
CREATE TABLE stg.deposit_book AS
SELECT
    deposit_id,
    counterparty_type,
    balance_eur,
    -- base (unstressed) 30-day runoff rate by counterparty
    CASE counterparty_type
        WHEN 'retail_insured'   THEN 0.05
        WHEN 'retail_uninsured' THEN 0.10
        WHEN 'operational'      THEN 0.25
        ELSE 0.40
    END                        AS base_runoff_rate,
    product_type
FROM raw.deposits;

-- 03_lcr_summary.sql  ·  aggregate HQLA and stressed outflows
CREATE TABLE lcr_summary AS
SELECT
    o.stress_scenario                         AS scenario,
    h.total_hqla_eur,
    SUM(o.outflow_eur)                        AS total_net_outflows_eur,
    h.total_hqla_eur
      / NULLIF(SUM(o.outflow_eur), 0)         AS lcr_ratio
FROM work.outflows_by_deposit o
CROSS JOIN (
    SELECT SUM(hqla_value_eur) AS total_hqla_eur
    FROM stg.hqla_securities
    WHERE eligible_flag = 1
) h
GROUP BY o.stress_scenario, h.total_hqla_eur;

-- 04_corep_c72_report.sql  ·  COREP C72.00 template
CREATE TABLE corep_c72_lcr AS
SELECT
    scenario,
    total_hqla_eur,
    total_net_outflows_eur          AS net_outflows_eur,
    ROUND(lcr_ratio * 100, 2)       AS lcr_ratio_pct
FROM lcr_summary;

tableEdges.reason: Per-deposit stressed outflow is computed in a SAS DATA step; the base runoff rate is scaled by a runtime stress multiplier (&mult) that is selected at execution, so the static parser cannot bind the per-row formula — this is where AI + a manual review of the run logs and ALM scenario catalogue close the gap.
The active stress scenario and its runoff multiplier are chosen at runtime inside the SAS macro via a macro variable; the selection and scaling logic is not statically visible.
